* 6. subtype?
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: types/subtype?
:FILE: src/graphden/types/core.clj
:LINE: 1224
:MINS: 13.7
:END:

The heart of assignability: reflexive / transitive subtyping across primitives, ~:jsonb~ sinks, records, lists, maps, tuples, refinements, unions, secrets, and fn-types. Every checker decision — is ~actual~ a subtype of ~expected~? — bottoms out here.

It is one ~cond~ ladder and the ORDER is the semantics: the universal yes/no arms first (identity, ~:any~, ~:never~, the typevar → ~:jsonb~ escape), then the ~:empty-map~ sentinel, unions (EVERY member on the left, SOME member on the right), primitives, ~:jsonb~, refinements, the structural shapes, and the ~:secret~ marker last. Don't hold the whole ladder in your head — find the arm for the pair of shapes you are asking about and read the comment that argues for it.

- source :: [[file:../../../src/graphden/types/core.clj::(defn subtype?][src/graphden/types/core.clj:1224]]

* 8. unify
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: types/unify
:FILE: src/graphden/types/core.clj
:LINE: 1652
:MINS: 10.1
:END:

Robinson unification with occurs-check and subtype-aware leniency, plus a union fallback. This is how polymorphic type variables get bound during checking — the two-way complement to the one-way ~subtype?~ test.

Same shape as ~subtype?~, so read it the same way: one ~cond~ over the normalised pair — typevar arms bind first (with the occurs check), then structural recursion into fn / list / record shapes, then the union fallback. It returns a substitution map or the ~::fail~ sentinel that ~unify-ok?~ / ~unify-fail?~ just below test for.

- source :: [[file:../../../src/graphden/types/core.clj::(defn unify][src/graphden/types/core.clj:1652]]

The single source of truth for nullability narrowing: remove ~:null~ from a top-level union (bare ~:null~ → ~:never~) while NEVER stripping a ~:secret~. The canonical example of type narrowing, shared by control-flow refinement and the ~:coalesce~ rule.

* 13. signature-return
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: types/signature-return
:FILE: src/graphden/types/check.clj
:LINE: 2135
:MINS: 4.0
:END:

The declared-signature engine: when a root base-fn has no hand ~:return-type-rule~, the polymorphic declaration itself computes the return — unify each var-carrying declared arg against the actual type at the site, resolve the declared return through the substitution. ~:coll [:list a] → [:union :null a]~ IS the rule; the hand-written rules that survive are only those reading literal values, union fan-out, or the registry.

- source :: [[file:../../../src/graphden/types/check.clj::(defn signature-return][src/graphden/types/check.clj:2135]]

Type-checks a single fn-def against its (single or multiple- inheritance) parents: resolve parent slots, run the monotonicity / unknown-slot / effect guards, unify bindings, compute the return via type-rules, propagate effects, and snapshot the rich-type into the registry. The per-node checker the sweep repeats.

* 16. record-rich-types!
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: types/record-rich-types!
:FILE: src/graphden/executor/registry/core.clj
:LINE: 438
:MINS: 10.4

Where the sweep's answers are KEPT. The rich-types registry is the in-memory ~{fn → {:return :args :effects …}}~ map every downstream consumer reads: the compiler's HOF-wrap decision, the executor's effect gate, secret redaction on persist, the editor's type chips. BRANCH-SCOPED since 2026-08-31: writes land on the ACTIVE atom — the global for the default branch, a per-ctx fork for every other (bound by the branch router at build + dispatch), so ~/api/types~ answers per branch instead of last-compile-wins. Aliases resolve to their structural body here, so everyone downstream sees one canonical shape.

- source :: [[file:../../../src/graphden/executor/registry/core.clj::(defn record-rich-types!][src/graphden/executor/registry/core.clj:438]]

…and how it is READ — by fn *id*, not name. Names are per-namespace labels and may repeat; ids cannot (docs/adr/ADR-identity-model.md, enforced in CI by ~id_resolution_guard_test~). The ~:by-name~ index survives only for base-fns and legacy call sites. Before you key any new registry or dispatch by name, read the ADR — this is the mistake it exists to stop.
